title: Minimum Window Substring
kidExplanation: Smallest window of s that still covers every required character from t (with counts).
plainProblem: Minimum Window Substring: Smallest window of s that still covers every required character from t (with counts). Worked example — input: s = "ADOBECODEBANC", t = "ABC"; expected output: "BANC". Why: Smallest cover. Interview pattern to name out loud: Sliding window.

thinkingSteps.title: Brute force idea
thinkingSteps.body: For “Minimum Window Substring”, first say a correct slow approach: scan or retry every candidate until the example works by hand. Input s = "ADOBECODEBANC", t = "ABC" should still produce "BANC".

thinkingSteps.title: Why it is slow
thinkingSteps.body: Count the nested work. If each choice restarts a full scan, time blows up. Name the cost before optimizing — interviewers want that honesty. Target after the insight: O(n).

thinkingSteps.title: Aha insight
thinkingSteps.body: To find the minimum window in the input string 's' that contains all characters from another string 't', we can use the sliding window approach. We first create a frequency dictionary for characters in 't'. Then, we initialize two pointers, 'left' and 'right', to represent the current window in 's'. As we move the 'right' pointer to the right, we add the character to a temporary frequency dictionary and check if it contains all characters from 't'. If it does, it means we found a valid window containing all characters from 't'. We update the minimum window length and move the 'left' pointer to the right to shrink the window. We continue this process until we find the minimum window or reach the end of 's'.

thinkingSteps.body: Commit to Sliding window. Longest/shortest subarray or substring with a condition. Walk example `s = "ADOBECODEBANC", t = "ABC"` → `"BANC"` while naming each variable, then code. Close with O(n) time and O(k) space.
